status: PROVISIONAL — NOT GOVERNING. First-pass Gate 3.1 batch-1 review decisions. Pending independent review and owner sign-off. Records §14A classification and §14C HP-1/HP-2 findings per field, and threshold provenance per literal. It clears nothing: no field is admitted as Layer-1 authority by this file, and Gate 3.2/3.3 are not started.

scope.layering: Gate 3A says what authority-relevant code exists and where. Gate 3.1 (this file) says what the batch-1 consumers are and how they classify under §14A, with first-pass §14C findings. Gate 3.2 (§14B decomposition) and Gate 3.3 (§14C test and provenance) are not started. Nothing here is a semantic clearance of the consumer map.

rules: Provenance is recorded only where a document or measurement establishes it. Otherwise it is UNKNOWN. It is never inferred from the numeric value or from what the value appears to mean.
A declared status in the artifact (for example RESEARCH_REFERENCE_NOT_CALIBRATED) is recorded as declaredStatus. It is not provenance.

HP-2 is PASS only where there is no tunable threshold (a domain boundary or set membership). Where the threshold's source is UNKNOWN, HP-2 is NOT_ESTABLISHED, not PASS and not FAIL. Gate 3.3 resolves it. Until then §14B ('Ambiguity resolves toward the feature vector, never toward state authority') means none of these thresholds is admitted state authority.

Correction to the worksheet template: its earlier line 'per HP-6, UNKNOWN moves the field downstream' over-read HP-6, which moves a field downstream for failing HP-1 or HP-2. At Gate 3.1, UNKNOWN provenance is a finding (HP-2 NOT_ESTABLISHED), not a failure. Gate 3.3 decides the consequence. The template line is corrected in tools/build-batch1.js; the worksheet JSON is unchanged.
A worksheet entry is a sink record, not a distinct source location. The 101 entries are 62 distinct (owner, expression) sites, and decisions are keyed by site so repeated entries get the same answer.
Each literal is assigned to the field whose threshold it actually is (belongsTo). A field listed against a site whose literals all belong elsewhere is a consumer there, not an owner.

classification.scope: The field as named is a composite of stop side and stop width/buffer. Only the stop-side/completeness part is confirmed as a hard-predicate candidate. The width and buffer limits are not.

hp1.basis: Field level: HP-6 gives no partial credit, and the width limits (STOP_TOO_WIDE > 3 ATR, maxStopATR per setup) fail because a wide stop is still structurally valid; it degrades payoff. Sub-predicate STOP_WRONG_SIDE (risk ≤ 0 or stop not beyond entry) passes HP-1: it is structural invalidity. The floors STOP_TOO_TIGHT (max(5 ticks, 0.2 ATR)), the planTradeLevels minimum max(10 × spec.p (minTickBuffer default), 0.25 ATR), and the buffers are NOT_ESTABLISHED: a stop inside tick or spread noise may be execution infeasibility, but nothing records the derivation.

That is an HP-2 risk the reviewer must rule on. The TTI_GEOMETRY tables carry no status.

decision.consequence: Split. STOP_WRONG_SIDE goes forward as a Layer-1 structural predicate (HP-1 PASS, HP-2 PASS: no tunable threshold) for Gate 3.3.
